conclusion.rationale: The patch changes the default lloadd feature set: proxyauthz is now enabled by default (LLOAD_FEATURE_PROXYAUTHZ via LLOAD_FEATURES_DEFAULT). Previously lload_features was zero-initialized (no features). This SIDE_EFFECT_CHANGE is confirmed by gdb variable inspection (BEFORE: $1=0, AFTER: $1=LLOAD_FEATURE_PROXYAUTHZ), gcov coverage (config_feature function switch/case executed 3x, new default initialization confirmed), and config parsing tests (enable/disable/feature keywords all work correctly). Deployments that rely on proxyauthz being OFF by default will experience a behavioral change: the Proxy Authorization control will now be sent to backend servers on every proxied operation. Backend servers that do not support this control may reject operations if the control is marked critical. Additionally, SASL-bind deployments now require backend servers to support the Who Am I? extended operation. A MEDIUM-priority finding (config schema attribute rename) was not tested per priority filter. Runtime LDAP traffic testing blocked by sandbox socket restriction.
recommended_actions: Review all existing lloadd deployments: if backend servers do not support Proxy Authorization control, add 'disable proxyauthz' to lloadd configs
